note: An experiment (GAME_SPEC §13.7, Stage 85; docs/CURRICULUM.md, experiment 42) on data/benches/lechatelier.json: Le Chatelier's principle on three equilibria, each tube held against one left as it is; the report's answers picked from choices, their truth read from the tubes.
title: Experiment: Le Chatelier's principle

report.label: more iron(III): the equilibrium went
report.why: More of a reactant: the equilibrium takes some of it away, making more of the complex. The tube is a deeper red than the one as it is, though both were diluted alike.

report.label: more thiocyanate: the equilibrium went
report.why: The same with the other reactant: SCN- added is partly taken up as FeSCN2+ (and some Fe(SCN)2+).

report.label: acid on chromate: the equilibrium went
report.why: Hydrogen ions are a reactant of 2 CrO4 2- + 2 H+ <=> Cr2O7 2- + H2O: added, the yellow turns orange. A base would take them away and turn it back.

report.label: warmed cobalt: the equilibrium went
report.why: Warming favours the way that takes in heat: the warm tube is bluer than the cool one, so pink to blue absorbs heat.

report.label: so pink to blue
report.why: Le Chatelier: a rise in temperature shifts an equilibrium the way that absorbs heat. Its enthalpy here, about +23 kJ/mol (ThermoChimie's for CoCl4 2-).

steps.title: Three tubes of the red
steps.text: Pick up the beaker of iron(III) thiocyanate, right-click the tube "red: as it is", type 5 and click "pour". The same into the tubes "more iron(III)" and "more thiocyanate".
steps.why: Fe3+ + SCN- <=> FeSCN2+: the red is the complex. One tube is kept as it is, to hold the others against.

steps.title: More iron(III)
steps.text: Pick up the iron(III) nitrate, right-click the tube "more iron(III)", type 0.5 and click "pour". Hold it against the one as it is.

steps.title: More thiocyanate
steps.text: Pick up the potassium thiocyanate, right-click the tube "more thiocyanate", type 0.5 and click "pour".

steps.title: Two tubes of chromate
steps.text: Pick up the potassium chromate, right-click the tube "chromate: as it is", type 5 and click "pour". The same into "chromate: acid added".
steps.why: 2 CrO4 2- + 2 H+ <=> Cr2O7 2- + H2O: chromate is yellow, dichromate orange.

steps.title: Acid
steps.text: Pick up the hydrochloric acid, right-click the tube "chromate: acid added", type 1 and click "pour".

steps.title: Two tubes of the cobalt
steps.text: Pick up the cobalt chloride in acid, right-click the tube "cobalt: at the room's 20 C", type 5 and click "pour". The same into "cobalt: warmed".
steps.why: Co(H2O)6 2+ + 4 Cl- <=> CoCl4 2- + 6 H2O: the pink hydrated ion and the blue chloro complex, both there in so much chloride: a violet.

steps.title: One into the warm bath
steps.text: Pick up the tube "cobalt: warmed", then right-click the bath. In the menu, click "stand it in". Then click 10x on the clock.

steps.title: Until it is warm
steps.text: Watch the tube in the bath as it warms, and hold it against the other.
